title: Indices
cover_sub: Powers follow rules, and the rules never change. Secure the three laws, extend to negative and fractional powers, then master equations where the unknown is in the power.

levels_long.s: The three laws: multiply, divide, power of a power.
levels_long.e: Zero, negative and fractional indices, brackets, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Unknowns in the power, and writing everything with one base.

briefing: When you multiply powers of the same base, add the indices. When you divide, subtract them. A power of a power: multiply them.
A negative index means one over: a−n = 1 ÷ an. A fractional index means a root: a1/n is the nth root, and am/n is the nth root, raised to the power m. Anything to the power 0 is 1.
method: Deal with numbers and letters separately.
Apply one law at a time, writing each step.
For a fractional index, take the root first: the numbers stay small.
For an index equation, write both sides as powers of the same base, then set the indices equal.

s.blurb: The method, step by step. Show every line.

questions.working: Multiply the numbers, add the indices.

text: Write 2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>4</sup> ÷ 2<sup>2</sup> as a single power of 2, then work out its value.

e.blurb: A step is hidden, or there's a context to unpick. One piece of tampered evidence.

text: Write as fractions: (a) 5−2 (b) (23)−1
questions.working: A negative index flips the fraction.
Every factor inside is raised to the power 4.
questions.tip: The 2 is raised to the power 4 as well: 2⁴ = 16, not 8.

text: Sara simplified (3x2)3. Find her mistake and give the correct answer.

m.blurb: No hints. Plan before you calculate.

questions.tip: Write both sides as powers of the same base. 9 and 27 are both powers of 3.

text: Evaluate (278)−2/3. Give your answer as a fraction.

closed_points: Multiply, divide and raise powers using the three laws.
Work with zero and negative indices.
Evaluate fractional indices by taking the root first.
Simplify expressions with numbers, letters and brackets.
Solve equations by writing both sides with the same base.
